program_plain: World: 400 self-propelled agents moving in a wrap-around 20x20 square. Rules each step: each agent turns away from agents within distance 1; otherwise it aligns with agents between 1 and 2 and moves toward agents between 2 and 15, ignoring agents in a 90-degree blind zone behind it; speed 3, turning rate limited to 40 degrees per step, heading noise 0.05 rad.
model_family: Zonal self-propelled particle / collective motion model (Aoki-Couzin; repulsion-alignment-attraction zones with blind zone), 2D periodic variant
standard_name: Couzin model torus (milling) state / vortex; swarm-torus-dynamic parallel-highly parallel transitions
citations: Couzin, Krause, James, Ruxton, Franks 2002, J. Theor. Biol. 218(1):1-11 - original model; torus/milling state with low polarization and high angular momentum when alignment zone small and attraction zone large; alignment-width transitions and hysteresis

Newman & Sayama 2008, Phys. Rev. E 78:011913 - effect of sensory blind zones on milling in a self-propelled particle model
Tunstrom et al. 2013, PLoS Comput Biol - milling, polarized and swarm states with multistability in schooling fish and Couzin-type models (year/authors not verified from search result)
Calovi et al., arXiv 1308.2889 - phase diagram of swarming/schooling/milling in a data-driven fish model (authors not verified from search result)
searches: Couzin 2002 Collective memory and spatial sorting in animal groups torus milling zone of repulsion orientation attraction

notes: Original Couzin model is 3D open space; this is 2D periodic with attraction range (15) exceeding half the box (10), so wrap-around and near-global attraction may shift quantitative phase boundaries; qualitative milling is expected. full_text:
**Verdict: KNOWN. This is the Couzin/Aoki zonal model, and its milling ("torus") state is a standard result.**

**1. Model family.** The system is a zonal self-propelled-particle or collective-motion model, the kind used for fish schools and bird flocks. Each agent has a zone of repulsion (r < 1), orientation or alignment (1–2) and attraction (2–15). There is also a rear blind zone, a limited turning rate, constant speed and angular noise. This is the Aoki (1982) / Couzin et al. (2002) model. Your settings (turning rate 40°, 90° blind zone, i.e. a field of perception of 270°) match the Couzin parameter set. A later paper that reuses this parameter set describes it as θ = 270° and ω = 40°/s (Jung, Brown & Goodrich 2013).

**2. The specific behaviour.** Milling, with low polar order and high angular momentum, is one of the four named states of the model. Couzin et al. describe the torus as individuals perpetually rotating around an empty core, with low group polarization and high angular momentum. It occurs when the orientation zone is relatively small and the attraction zone relatively large. Your readings (milling 6.5, polar 0.1, clumped 0.3) fit this. Clumping would be expected because the attraction zone is so large.

The "alignment zone up to 2.5" variant is also covered. Couzin et al. varied the orientation-zone width and reported major group-level behavioural transitions from minor changes in individual-level interactions. They also reported hysteresis, which they call collective memory. Near the swarm/torus/parallel boundaries, a small change in alignment width can therefore flip the state. This explains why the 2.0 and 2.5 variants might both mill, or might differ.

**3. Citations, checked against search results.**
- **Earliest clear source:** Couzin, Krause, James, Ruxton & Franks (2002), "Collective memory and spatial sorting in animal groups", *J. Theor. Biol.* 218(1):1–11, doi:10.1006/jtbi.2002.3065. The Bath, Bristol and Semantic Scholar records confirm the bibliographic details. The full-text PDF shows the swarm / torus / dynamic parallel / highly parallel classification.
- **Review:** "Collective behavior in animal groups: theoretical models and empirical studies" (PMC2639936). It summarises Couzin et al. as giving swarm-like aggregations, toroidal milling groups, and coherent dynamic groups. I did not verify the authors, year or venue of this review from the search result, so check those before citing it.
- **Related work (all seen in search results):**
  - Newman & Sayama (2008), *Phys. Rev. E* 78:011913, "The Effect of Sensory Blind Zones on Milling Behavior in a Dynamic Self-Propelled Particle Model" (arXiv 0711.3253). It studies how blind zones affect milling, though in a force-based model rather than a zonal one.
  - Tunstrøm et al., *PLoS Comput Biol* (2013), "Collective States, Multistability and Transitional Behavior in Schooling Fish". It shows milling, polarized and swarm states, and multistability. I did not verify the year or author list from the search results.
  - Calovi et al., arXiv 1308.2889, "Swarming, Schooling, Milling: Phase diagram of a data-driven fish school model". I did not verify the authors from the search results.

**4. Differences that probably don't matter.**
- Couzin et al. worked in 3D in open space, whereas this is a 2D periodic box. In 2D the torus becomes a rotating vortex or mill, which Newman & Sayama and Calovi et al. describe.
- The box is 20×20 and the attraction range is 15, which exceeds half the box width. Attraction is therefore nearly global and wrap-around images interact. Milling is still expected, but this could change the exact phase boundaries. I did not find a source treating that specific regime.
- The "5 distinct rule programs" are most likely parameter points in the same Couzin phase diagram.

**5. Confidence: high.** The model structure, parameter values and the milling signature (low polarization, high rotation) all match the well-known Couzin phase diagram. Several independent reviews and follow-up papers confirm it. The remaining uncertainty is quantitative: the exact thresholds for this box and these parameters are not something I looked up.

**Searches run:**
1. Couzin 2002 collective memory, torus, zones of repulsion/orientation/attraction.
2. Blind zone, turning rate, milling vortex, Couzin model torus, dynamic parallel group.
